findings.observed: The stderr helper writes and flushes the retained log inside a broad `except BaseException: return`. A write or flush error therefore terminates the helper silently. `close_and_join()` subsequently hashes the possibly partial file and reports its path/digest without an error; normal process cleanup can then retain `helpers_stopped: true` and return a successful outcome.
findings.expected: A write/flush failure in the required MCP stderr sink must be retained as a log failure and prevent a success/complete-log claim; retained path/digest evidence is valid only after every captured stderr byte has been persisted and the sink closes successfully.
findings.reproduction: Use a file-like stderr log whose write or flush raises after accepting an initial chunk. `_stderr()` catches and discards that exception at controller.py:208-217. On teardown, controller.py:169-184 closes and hashes the truncated file, and controller.py:450-463 sees no `cleanup_error` from the transport, allowing the normal success path to continue.
findings.impact: A physical MCP call can be marked successful with a retained, hash-bound but incomplete server log, defeating the accepted C0 requirement that server stderr diagnostics and log-completeness failures remain auditable and fail closed.
findings.no_fix_consequence: C3/C4 may accept misleading server-log evidence precisely when filesystem failure drops MCP diagnostics, leaving no durable signal that the declared log boundary was incomplete.
findings.smallest_fix: Record stderr writer/flush exceptions in synchronized transport state; have `close_and_join()` expose that state as a cleanup error and refuse a complete digest claim, so existing controller cleanup releases the exact claim and raises. Add one focused fake-sink write/flush-failure assertion.
findings.complexity: Low and local to the new stderr transport state.
findings.regression_risk: Low: it changes only failed log persistence into a fail-closed controller result; stdout framing, launch arguments, lane binding, and cleanup ownership remain unchanged.
findings.verification_cost: Low host-only transport/controller coverage; no MCP server or hardware is required.
findings.alternatives: Treating a digest of the truncated file as sufficient leaves the precise evidence boundary untrustworthy; external log handling would violate controller-only ownership.
findings.cost_benefit: The direct false-completeness risk outweighs this contained error-propagation change and its focused verification cost.
